text: US stocks recovered most of a steep early AI-driven sell-off on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 down 0.3% to 7,182.78 after falling as much as 3.2% intraday, the Nasdaq down 0.6% to 23,585.80, and the Dow up 0.3% to about 50,183 after reversing a drop of more than 1,100 points. Nvidia fell about 4% and chip stocks such as Lam Research and Micron lost 4% to 6%, while October core PCE inflation came in at 3.3% against 3.2% expected and Brent crude rose 3.5% to $94.61. The S&P 500 is still up about 3.9% for the week, and most of its members rose even as the index slipped. The TSX closed at about 34,180, up 0.64%, after an early drop of nearly 600 points. In Europe the STOXX 600 closed down about 1% at 626.03, with banks down about 3%, while in Asia the Nikkei fell 2.8%, the Kospi 6.2%, Taiwan's Taiex 4.8% and the Hang Seng about 1.1%; FTSE, DAX and other closes could not be confirmed.
mood: AI and chip stocks sold off sharply again, with hot inflation data, rate-hike expectations, tariffs and higher oil adding pressure, though Wall Street recovered most of its early losses.

veqt.t: S&P 500 -0.3%, Nasdaq -0.6%, Dow +0.3%, as Nvidia and chip stocks fell but the Dow and small caps rose.
TSX rose about 0.64% to roughly 34,180 after recovering from an early drop of nearly 600 points.
STOXX 600 fell about 1% to 626.03 with banks down about 3% and tech lower again; Nikkei fell 2.8%, while FTSE, DAX and ASX 200 closes were not confirmed.
Hang Seng fell about 1.1%, Kospi 6.2% and Taiex 4.8% as Asian chip stocks gave back gains; Shanghai fell about 2% (single source) and Hang Seng Tech was not confirmed.

label: Mixed today
